answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. This is resilient because unearned rewards are capped and eventually burned, so an attacker cannot bank on a runaway Sybil campaign paying off. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a bridge as the anchor of the cost.
